correctness.rationale: For every C1 nonnegative recruitment response F near K>0 with F(K)=K and a=F'(K)<1, the exact Jacobian is [[ag,a(1-g)],[1,0]]. Strict quadratic Jury gives 1-a>0, 1+a(2g-1)>0 and 1+a(1-g)>0. Solving these inequalities for all a and 0<=g<=1 yields the complete four-case phase diagram. For q=-a>1 the interval is 1-1/q<g<(1+1/q)/2 and nonempty iff q<3. At q=3,g=2/3 the matrix has a double -1 and nonzero square-zero nilpotent part; the exact power law follows. Ricker derivative equals 1-r. The standalone check.py has 3554 passing exact-rational/numerical subsidiary assertions. The proof, not testing, covers all parameters; nonlinear boundary stability is deliberately not claimed.

value.rationale: Two adjacent breeding cohorts form the smallest biologically natural delay-allocation design. The exact complete derivative–allocation phase answers whether a given overcompensatory recruitment response admits ANY locally stabilizing cohort mixture, shows exactly how the allowed choice collapses, and identifies the unique nonsemisimple transient boundary. This is a structural all-parameter benchmark rather than a few numerical examples or a mere reparametrization; it is explicitly limited to the chosen cohort-separable mechanism.
